name: Niger
tagline: The Air, the Tenere, and the last giraffes of West Africa
summary: The Tenere is the emptiest desert on earth, the Air massif rises out of it to two thousand metres, and the last West African giraffes live wild an hour from the capital.
when: November to February. The Air and Tenere need current advice and local guides.

entries.caption: The Tenere
entries.description: Four hundred thousand square kilometres of sand with nothing in it at all.
entries.subject: the empty dune field of the Tenere desert under a low sun

entries.caption: The Air Massif
entries.description: Granite mountains standing two thousand metres out of the sand, with guelta pools in them.
entries.subject: the granite peaks of the Air massif rising from desert sand

entries.caption: The Last West African Giraffe
entries.description: About six hundred of them at Kouré, the only wild population left in the whole of West Africa.
entries.subject: West African giraffe browsing among bush near Kouré

entries.caption: W National Park
entries.description: Shared with Benin and Burkina Faso — lion, elephant and buffalo on the Niger river.
entries.subject: elephants in tall grass in W National Park

entries.caption: Mont Idoukal-n-Taghes
entries.description: 2,022 metres in the Air, and the high point of a range full of rock art.
entries.subject: a granite peak in the Air massif with a palm-filled valley below

entries.caption: Guelta Pools
entries.description: Permanent rock pools in the Air, the only standing water for hundreds of kilometres.
entries.subject: a permanent rock pool with palms in the Air mountains

entries.caption: The Niger at Niamey
entries.description: The river runs 550 kilometres across the southwest and the whole country leans on it.
entries.subject: pirogues on the Niger river at Niamey at sunset

entries.caption: Sandbars on the River
entries.description: Landlocked, and the swimming is off the sandbanks at Niamey when the river is low.
entries.subject: a wide sandbar in the Niger river with people on it

entries.caption: The Doum Palm Valleys
entries.description: Palm-filled wadis in the Air, green lines through absolutely bare rock.
entries.subject: doum palms filling a wadi between bare granite in the Air

entries.caption: Crossing the Tenere
entries.description: The Tree of Tenere marked the crossing until a truck hit it in 1973. The route is still run.
entries.subject: a four-wheel-drive convoy crossing the empty Tenere sand

entries.caption: Tuareg, Hausa, Zarma, Fulani
entries.description: Tuareg and Toubou in the north, Hausa and Zarma in the south, Wodaabe in between.
entries.subject: a Tuareg man in indigo leading a camel in the Air

entries.caption: The Wodaabe
entries.description: The Gerewol, where the men dress and dance and the women choose.
entries.subject: Wodaabe men in face paint dancing at the Gerewol

entries.caption: Millet, Djerma Rice and Kilishi
entries.description: Millet paste with sauce, and kilishi — beef dried thin and spiced, the best in the region.
entries.subject: strips of spiced kilishi dried beef on a rack

entries.caption: The Cure Salee
entries.description: Tuareg and Wodaabe gather at In-Gall in September when the salt pastures come up.
entries.subject: camels and tents gathered at the Cure Salee festival at In-Gall

entries.caption: Tuareg Silver and Leather
entries.description: The Agadez cross in silver, and camel saddles and boxes in tooled leather.
entries.subject: silver Agadez crosses laid out on tooled leather

entries.caption: Agadez
entries.description: A mud minaret twenty-seven metres high, and the Sultanate that has stood behind it since 1449.
entries.subject: the tall mud minaret of the Agadez mosque with its wooden beams

entries.caption: Three Sites
entries.description: Agadez, the Air and Tenere reserves, and W National Park — desert, mountain and river.
entries.subject: prehistoric rock engravings of cattle in the Air mountains

entries.caption: Niamey and Agadez
entries.description: A river capital with the best museum in the Sahel, and a caravan city at the desert edge.
entries.subject: the mud-brick old quarter of Agadez at street level

entries.caption: Mud and Beams
entries.description: Sahelian mud with projecting timber, and the Agadez minaret as its tallest expression.
entries.subject: the beamed mud tower of the Agadez minaret against the sky

entries.caption: The Niamey Grand Marche
entries.description: Everything from millet to motorcycle parts, and the noise that goes with it.
entries.subject: the crowded aisles of the Grand Marche in Niamey

entries.caption: Giraffes an Hour Away
entries.description: Kouré is a morning trip from Niamey, on foot, and children can do it.
entries.subject: a family on foot watching giraffe browse at Kouré

entries.caption: The Air on Foot and Camel
entries.description: Weeks of walking or riding between guelta and village, with Tuareg guides.
entries.subject: a camel caravan crossing sand below the Air mountains

entries.caption: Very Little
entries.description: A few hotels in Niamey. Everything north is camps and hospitality.
entries.subject: a courtyard hotel terrace in Niamey at dusk

entries.caption: Giraffes Beside Farms
entries.description: Kouré's giraffes live among fields, and the community is paid to keep it that way.
entries.subject: giraffe walking past millet fields and a farmer at Kouré

entries.caption: Dunes and Nothing
entries.description: The Tenere at either end of the day, where the only vertical thing is your own shadow.
entries.subject: long shadows across a bare dune field in the Tenere

entries.caption: The Bilma Salt Caravans
entries.description: The azalai still runs from Agadez to Bilma and back, a thousand kilometres by camel.
entries.subject: a salt caravan of camels crossing dunes near Bilma

entries.caption: Why Niger
entries.description: The emptiest desert on earth, and a giraffe population saved by the people farming next to it.
entries.subject: a giraffe standing against open Sahelian sky at Kouré
